mathematical_findings_container.note: frozen mathematical evidence records; this container adds ML context and never modifies them

reference.framing: reference-product labels; agreement metrics are NOT ground-truth accuracy

features.resolution_note: blue/green/red/nir native 10 m; swir16 native 20 m bilinearly resampled to the 10 m analysis grid by the audited pipeline (no native 10 m SWIR)

split_design.method: contiguous 100-px block row stripes: train/validation/test interleaved bands
split_design.design_note: deterministic blocking concentrates rare classes unevenly across folds; per-class test support is reported and metrics are gated at support < 50 px

water.support_note: test support 0 < 50: per-class metrics not interpretable and not reported (label-gate rule)

evaluation.framing: agreement with the ESA WorldCover v200 reference product on spatially separated test blocks; NOT independent ground-truth accuracy

geographic_stability.note: agreement spread across geographically different held-out blocks; a wide range means the classifier does not generalise uniformly over the AOI

earlier.note: model probabilities are confidences, not accuracy estimates

later.note: model probabilities are confidences, not accuracy estimates

math_baseline_comparison.note: predicted class-fraction shifts between the two epochs compared against the mathematical Δ-index finding; both are candidate signals, neither is treated as verification

ml_record.plain_language: A Random Forest trained on 2021 reference labels (ESA WorldCover) reproduces that reference on held-out test blocks at 85% overall agreement. Applied to the two measured composites, the predicted class mix shifts: built_up +19.0 pp; vegetation −11.9 pp. These are model predictions against reference-product labels — not independent ground truth and not verified change.
interpretation_guardrails: No claim of independent ground-truth accuracy is permitted.
Predicted fractions are model outputs on reference-inherited class definitions.
Application to 2020/2025 assumes class-spectral stability across epochs (limitation, not verified).

limitations: Reference labels are ESA WorldCover v200, itself a classification product; all metrics measure agreement with it, not ground truth.
Applying the 2021-trained classifier to 2020/2025 composites assumes class-spectral stability across epochs.
Rare classes below the 50-px test-support floor are not reported rather than estimated.
Class-prediction probabilities are confidences, never accuracy.
